**Would you like to lead the development of cutting-edge audiology that improves life for millions of people with hearing loss worldwide?

**In this role, you will work at the heart of Demant’s innovation, leading the group that creates the world-leading audiological technology used across Demant hearing aids.

**The Role

**As Director, you will lead the leaders and teams that make up the Audio group—an organization of 75 highly skilled experts. Through your leadership team, you will be accountable for strengthening R&D delivery and ensuring that the organization has the skills, culture, capacity, structure, and ways of working required to succeed.

You will set direction, develop leaders, and enable teams to perform at their best. Building on a strong existing organization and guided by the company strategy, you will prepare the organization for the future.

**Welcome to Audiological Solutions

**You will join a global R&D organization of more than 1,000 engineers and specialists across electronics, mechanics, software, acoustics, AI, and audiology—all working to improve hearing healthcare.

The Audio group is part of the Audiological Solutions department, one of the cornerstones of the Device Software area. We believe in collaboration, curiosity, openness, and diverse thinking. Your leadership will shape how we deliver, learn, and grow.

**Your Responsibilities

**Reporting to the Senior Director of Audiological Solutions, you will:

• Lead and develop an organization of 75 developers and leaders responsible for one of Demant’s core deliveries: world-leading audiology for Demant hearing solutions.

• Lead and develop leaders, providing clear direction and an inclusive environment where people can contribute and grow.

• Be accountable for R&D delivery through your leadership team and organization.

• Partner with SAFe ART leadership to create transparency, remove systemic barriers, and deliver value.

• Translate company strategy into clear priorities and action.

• Build the skills and competencies, and allocate the capacity, needed to deliver the roadmap and secure long-term success—with innovation as a key priority.

• Build a culture rooted in innovation, trust, collaboration, and the ambition to lead audiology.

• Lead organizational design, including recruitment, performance, development, engagement, and wellbeing.

• Improve workflows and strengthen learning and collaboration across organizational boundaries.

**About You

**You are an experienced people leader with a strong record of helping teams perform and grow. You have likely led leaders, either directly or indirectly. You create clarity, share accountability, and empower others to make decisions.

You communicate clearly, listen well, and build alignment across functions and organizational levels. You approach complex problems with curiosity and sound judgment, and you work effectively in a matrix organization.

You understand R&D delivery and can connect people, skills, capacity, quality, and ways of working with product and technology roadmaps. Familiarity with Lean-Agile leadership and SAFe is valuable, as is the ability to combine a strategic perspective with practical delivery insight.

You bring considerable leadership experience, hold a higher technical education, and have preferably experience within audiology or related areas. Fluency in English is required.

Interested?

To learn more about the role, contact Ole Fogh Olsen, Senior Director of Audiological Solutions, at oleo@demant.com.

Apply by November 1st 2026 through our online recruitment system.

We look forward to hearing from you.

_At Demant, we value diversity, equity, and inclusion (DE&I), and we are committed to creating an inclusive working environment. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of ethnic background, personality, age, gender, and education. Diversity is part of our cultural DNA. Women in STEM areas are particularly encouraged to apply, as Demant supports United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 5 on gender equality.

_Demant is a world leading hearing healthcare and technology group built on a heritage of care, health, and innovation since 1904. The Group offers innovative technologies, solutions, and expertise to enable people hear better. In every aspect, from hearing care, hearing aids and hearing implants to diagnostic equipment and services and audio solutions, Demant is active and engaged. Headquartered in Denmark, the Group employs more than 21,000 people globally and is present with solutions in 130 countries where we create life-changing hearing health and high-end audio and video solutions. William Demant Foundation holds the majority of shares in Demant A/S, which is listed on Nasdaq Copenhagen and among the 25 most traded stocks.

About MITS Industries

MITS Industries is an advanced systems and industrialization company developing integrated technology platforms for demanding aerospace, security, and mission-critical applications. Its mission is to transform operationally validated technologies into scalable, ready-to-deploy systems by combining advanced engineering, industrial partnerships, and strong governance.

MITS Industries is establishing an R&D and design site in Copenhagen focused on advanced RF systems, signal intelligence, aerospace technologies, and mission-critical product development. The site will build core capabilities in RF and microwave hardware, antenna systems, RF testing and characterization, rugged mechanical integration, and the industrialization of complex radio-electronic systems.

The Copenhagen team will work closely with strategic partners and engineering teams across Europe, playing a leading role in the development, validation, industrialization, and deployment of advanced technologies for defense, aerospace, and other demanding applications.

One of the initial focus areas will be an advanced aerospace signal-intelligence product platform covering RF and system architecture, antenna-system design, RF and microwave hardware, laboratory validation, mechanical integration, integration with the satellite platform, and preparation for qualification, production, and operational deployment.

The ambition is to build a strong technical design site capable of taking complex RF products, modules, and platforms from architecture and detailed design through prototyping, testing, validation, industrialization, and international deployment.

About the role

MITS Industries is looking for a Senior Mechanical Design Engineer to join the core Copenhagen R&D team and help build the site’s mechanical design capability for antenna and RF systems. The role is intended for an experienced mechanical engineer with prior hands-on experience developing the mechanical implementation of antenna, RF, or microwave hardware.

You will design and develop mechanical solutions for antenna systems and associated RF and electronic assemblies. The work includes antenna supports and mounts, RF-aware enclosures, radomes, fixed and, where applicable, deployable antenna mechanisms, test fixtures, thermal solutions, connector integration, cable routing, sealing, environmental protection, and platform interfaces. Many of these structures can directly affect antenna and RF performance, requiring close co-design with antenna and RF engineers.

The role covers mechanical architecture, material and manufacturing-process selection, structural and thermal analysis, tolerance definition, detailed CAD design, prototyping, assembly, environmental validation, serviceability, and production release. Particular attention will be given to mechanical structures that directly affect antenna performance, integration, alignment, stability, and deployment.

You will work closely with antenna systems engineers, RF and microwave hardware engineers, system architects, RF test and characterization engineers, manufacturing partners, and partner engineering teams. The role requires strong mechanical design expertise, RF-aware product thinking, end-to-end technical ownership, and hands-on implementation experience, taking designs from concept through prototype build and qualification to documented, manufacturable antenna assemblies and integrated systems.

Key responsibilities

• Translate system, antenna, and platform requirements into mechanical architectures, interface definitions, design constraints, and technical trade-offs.

• Design mechanical components and assemblies for antenna systems, including supports, mounts, frames, radomes, RF-aware enclosures, fixed or deployable mechanisms, and platform-integration structures.

• Own the detailed mechanical implementation of antenna and RF assemblies, including 3D CAD models, 2D manufacturing drawings, GD&T, assembly-level tolerance analysis, BOMs, and configuration-controlled documentation.

• Develop mechanical solutions that maintain antenna alignment, dimensional stability, RF clearances, grounding, shielding, cable routing, connector accessibility, and other mechanical conditions required to achieve the intended electromagnetic performance.

• Integrate RF modules, antennas, electronics, connectors, cables, gaskets, thermal interfaces, and environmental sealing into complete mechanical assemblies.

• Perform structural, thermal, and tolerance analyses covering stiffness, strength, mass properties, thermal expansion, heat transfer, vibration, shock, and expected environmental loads.

• Define mechanical requirements and work jointly with antenna and RF engineers to establish electromagnetic constraints for radomes, covers, supports, enclosures, and other structures located within or near the antenna field.

• Design antenna deployment and positioning mechanisms, where applicable, including hinges, latches, restraints, stops, alignment features, and associated interfaces.

• Design test fixtures, alignment tools, handling aids, assembly tooling, and prototype-support hardware for antenna and RF system development.

• Select materials, coatings, surface treatments, fasteners, adhesives, seals, bearings, and manufacturing processes based on structural, thermal, RF, environmental, corrosion, and production requirements.

• Lead mechanical prototype build, assembly, troubleshooting, design verification, and iterative improvement.

• Contribute to environmental testing and qualification, including vibration, shock, thermal cycling, ingress protection, and other relevant mechanical validation activities.

• Apply design-for-manufacture, design-for-assembly, serviceability, reliability, and cost considerations throughout development.

• Work with suppliers and manufacturing partners on technical clarification, process selection, prototype production, inspection, non-conformance resolution, and production release.

• Prepare mechanical specifications, analysis reports, interface-control documentation, design-review materials, assembly instructions, and production handover documentation.

• Collaborate with antenna, RF and microwave hardware, system, test, electronics, manufacturing, and partner engineering teams.

• Help establish mechanical design standards, CAD practices, documentation templates, and engineering workflows for the Copenhagen design site.

Required qualifications and experience

• Degree in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, or a related engineering discipline, or equivalent relevant professional experience.

• 5+ years of professional mechanical design experience, including demonstrated experience developing mechanical hardware for antenna, RF, or microwave systems where mechanical geometry, materials, interfaces, tolerances, or nearby structures directly influence electromagnetic performance.

• Strong hands-on experience and demonstrated technical ownership of complex mechanical assemblies from initial architecture and concept through detailed design, prototype build, verification, qualification, and production release.

• Advanced proficiency with a professional 3D CAD and drafting environment; SolidWorks experience is preferred.

• Strong command of GD&T, engineering drawing standards, assembly-level tolerance analysis, and production-quality mechanical documentation.

• Demonstrated experience designing mechanical components or assemblies for antenna, RF, or microwave systems, such as antenna supports and mounts, frames, enclosures, radomes, mechanisms, fixtures, or other mechanically and electromagnetically constrained structures.

• Experience with mechanical packaging and integration of antennas, RF modules, PCBs, connectors, cables, thermal interfaces, shielding, grounding, seals, and associated electronics.

• Practical understanding of RF-aware mechanical design, including the effects of materials, structures, clearances, alignment, grounding, shielding, cabling, and radomes on antenna and RF performance.

• Experience applying engineering calculations and simulation methods, including finite-element analysis where appropriate, to support structural and thermal design decisions.

• Understanding of stiffness, strength, thermal expansion, heat transfer, vibration, shock, fatigue, and other relevant environmental loads.

• Practical knowledge of metallic materials, engineering polymers, elastomers, composites, adhesives, coatings, and surface treatments.

• Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, such as precision machining, sheet-metal fabrication, additive manufacturing, composite manufacturing, joining, fastening, sealing, and assembly.

• Demonstrated hands-on experience with prototype assembly, mechanical troubleshooting, design verification, and iterative improvement.

• Experience supporting environmental testing and qualification, such as vibration, shock, thermal cycling, ingress protection, or comparable validation activities.

• Experience working with suppliers and manufacturing teams on process selection, technical clarification, inspection, non-conformance resolution, manufacturability, and production handover.

Nice to have

• Experience developing lightweight, stiffness-critical structures with stringent alignment and dimensional-stability requirements.

• Experience with aerospace or space-hardware qualification, including thermal-vacuum testing, outgassing constraints, vibration, and shock.

• Experience with precision mechanical alignment, dimensional inspection, antenna positioning, and calibration or verification fixtures.

• Experience designing IP-rated enclosures or ruggedized outdoor electronic equipment.

• Experience with product data management, configuration control, and release processes for complex mechanical assemblies.

• Experience working with international suppliers and manufacturing partners on low-volume, high-complexity hardware.

• Experience designing radomes, RF-transparent structures, or mechanical structures located within or near the antenna field.

• Experience with mechanically steerable, deployable, foldable, or position-critical antenna systems.

• Experience working directly with antenna or electromagnetic simulation engineers to iterate mechanical geometry, materials, and interfaces based on RF performance.

Success in the first 6 months

• Take end-to-end technical ownership of one or more mechanical subsystems or integration areas for antenna and RF systems.

• Establish the initial mechanical architecture, material and manufacturing approach, and platform-integration plan for the assigned scope.

• Deliver reviewed 3D models, manufacturing drawings, tolerance analyses, interface definitions, and supporting design documentation.

• Develop and support the build, assembly, and verification of initial mechanical prototypes, fixtures, or engineering models.

• Identify key structural, thermal, alignment, sealing, deployment, and manufacturability risks and define practical mitigation actions.

• Establish effective technical interfaces with antenna, RF and microwave hardware, system, test, electronics, manufacturing, supplier, and partner engineering teams.

• Help establish mechanical design standards, CAD practices, documentation templates, and release workflows for the Copenhagen design site.

**About The Role

**Genmab is seeking a Project Manager CMC Product Lifecycle Management to

• join the CMC Life Cycle Management (LCM) Team and support our growing portfolio of commercial products globally.

The LCM team is responsible for managing the CMC lifecycle activities of Genmab’s commercial products and manufacturing oversight, ensuring supply continuity, regulatory compliance, and successful execution of post-approval activities throughout the product lifecycle. In this role, you’ll work closely with LCM Product Lead and colleagues across Commercial Supply Chain, MSAT, Regulatory CMC, Commercial QA and External Manufacturing to ensure seamless execution of lifecycle management activities.

The CMC Life Cycle Management Team is part of CMC Project & Portfolio Management (PPM) which also includes the Early-Stage Development, Late-stage Development and External Manufacturing teams. CMC Project & Portfolio Management resides within CMC Development and Manufacturing, based in Denmark.

This role offers a unique opportunity to contribute to the continued growth of Genmab's commercial portfolio while working in a highly collaborative and cross-functional environment at the interface of development, manufacturing, supply, and regulatory affairs.

**Responsibilities

**

• Work alongside the LCM Lead to provide manufacturing oversight and execute lifecycle activities for an assigned manufacturing track (DS, BI, CI or DP) after commercial launch, supporting batch release and reliable supply. The LCM Lead retains overall product accountability.

• Lead operational governance with internal functions and partners/CMOs, aligning priorities, preparing decisions, tracking progress and actions, and providing input on CMO performance.

• Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders on daily operations to ensure manufacturing oversight (ie. Deviation management, change control, complaint handling, etc) , support batch release and supply, issues resolution/escalation and quality/regulatory compliance.

• Coordinate technical issue resolution and manage track risks with relevant experts, ensuring required assessments, documentation and mitigation actions, and escalating issues with proposed next steps.

• Drive manufacturing changes, projects and improvements within agreed scope, timelines and budgets.

• Support implementation of CMC commitments and Post-approval change management related to assigned product manufacturing track (i.e DS, BI, CI, DP) and support coordination of submission documentation preparation across stakeholders and CMOs/Partners.

• Support initiatives to optimize yield, reduce cost of goods, and enhance robustness of manufacturing and testing processes

• Help establish and improve LCM processes, governance, tools and ways of working, incorporating lessons learned.

**Requirements

**

• Master's degree in science or related technical discipline (e.g. engineering, biotech, pharmaceutical, biochemistry, biology) or equivalent experience;

• 4+ years of experience in biopharmaceutical industry, preferably within manufacturing operations, lifecycle, product management for commercial products.

• Experience in building relations and influencing multi-functional teams within multicultural organizations.

• Proven track record in CMC project management, manufacturing operations management or product management across development and commercialization activities.

• Experience managing and defining project coordination activities and tasks in a structured, regulated environment.

• Prior experience with commercial product lifecycle management and oversight of Contract Manufacturing Organizations (CMOs) is considered an advantage.

• Broad understanding of global cGMP requirements and regulatory expectations across major markets

• Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with fluency in English

• Demonstrated ability to work effectively in cross-functional and multicultural environments

• Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities, balance competing demands, and deliver against project timelines

• Team player with the ability to collaborate with diverse stakeholders.

• Result- and goal-oriented, committed to contributing to Genmab’s success

**Job Description

**Are you a self-starting transformation driver, strategic thinker and pragmatic deliverer, who turns a long-term vision and complex objectives into step-by-step reality and a clear path forward? Do you possess strong project management skills with the ability to translate a multi-year roadmap into smaller bricks and actionable wins, keeping momentum high as requirements evolve? Are you a gifted communicator who breaks down silos and unites cross-functional teams around a lean way of working? Do you possess the business acumen and analytical skills to spot risks and interdependencies across projects and complex organizations? **If so, join us as S&OP Project Manager!

****What The Job Is …

**We have embarked on a multi-year, enterprise-wide transformation program through 2030 to support the long-term growth and industrialization of Satair and Airbus Material Services. We are redesigning the Processes, Methods, Tools and Data (PMTD) across various domains and organizations, for a lean operating model powered by a Fit-to-Standard modern ERP and harmonized processes.

One of the key cornerstones of this transformation is the deployment of an integrated end-to-end Sales and Operations Planning process across various businesses.

In your position as S&OP Project Manager you will be part of a cross-functional and cross-organizational project team. In addition to designing and implementing the TO BE S&OP Processes, Methods, Tools and Data (PMTD), you will act as the key point between our external consultancy partners, internal business stakeholders and the broader enterprise transformation program.

_Travel required: 15%

_**How You Will Contribute To The Team

**

• PMTD and Architecture Design and Implementation: Design the target Process, Method, Tools and Data covering customer demand, supply capacity and feedback loop mechanisms, including scenario-planning and escalation protocols across and between businesses. Partner with IT and Digital to define the future ERP requirements for S&OP, ensuring a seamless and integrated architecture between Processes and Tools.

• Project Management: Define project roadmap, translate long-term ambition into short-term milestones, maintain project governance, ensure progress towards deliverables, identify and proactively manage interdependencies and risks.

• Stakeholder Alignment Beyond Silos: Proactively identify and engage senior stakeholders across functions and organizations in a complex environment to drive alignment on future ways of working, overcome organizational friction and secure global process simplification and standardization.

• Consultant Management: Lead the relationship with external consultants, steering their deliverables to shape our target S&OP Processes, Methods, Tools and Data (PMTD). Validate consultant proposals and recommendations against business needs and context, ensuring designs are scalable and implementable across various business units.

• Strategic Escalations & Executive Briefings: Prepare executive-ready decks, high-impact decision dossiers, trade-off analysis, recommendations and progress updates for executive forums and the central Transformation steering.

• ERP Fit-to-Standard (F2S): Drive business readiness and stakeholder participation across multi-functional teams for F2S workshops to design the future ERP requirements. Safeguard S&OP scope requirements within the central ERP system, ensuring seamless alignment between S&OP process and the future ERP capabilities.

• Ad-Hoc Initiatives: Lead other potential initiatives or projects related to S&OP.

**Candidate Profile & Qualifications

Core experience and background:

**

• Education: MSc/MA in Business, Economics, Strategy, Finance, Supply Chain or a related field

• Experience and Track record: 5-8+ years of experience in Project Management, Supply Chain, Management Consulting or equivalent. Proven track record in project management, S&OP deployment, leading cross-functional teams or enterprise process redesigns.

• Methodologies: Mastery of structured project management and business process mapping.

• Languages: Fluent English is mandatory. Good command of French or German is a plus.

**Work Style And Soft Skills

**

• You are self-driven, proactive and autonomous

• You can translate complex long-term objectives into clear sequential steps. You have a strong focus on driving progress and delivering results, ensuring execution momentum even when requirements change.

• You can balance strategic thinking with tactical execution

• You are analytical, and enjoy understanding the intricacies of how things work

• You are a natural communicator and consensus builder, with the ability to understand and demystify complex concepts to obtain stakeholder buy-in

• You have excellent analytical skills and business acumen, able to translate complex information into clear recommendations

You will build and run its engine keeping the Product and Marketing finance team connected to the financial heartbeat of the company: one planning calendar, one reporting standard, cost control across worldwide envelopes, and an automation toolchain that makes reporting produce itself. You are shaping how this team runs, and the role grows as the toolchain does. As we build the team capabilities, we continue delivering results every quarter, budget every autumn, and the value optimization discipline that funds our growth.

This is a role for someone who is a pace setter, taking real pride in a rhythm that builds credibility, and who wants to modernize how the work gets done.

**What You Will Do

**

• Own the Product and Marketing financial planning calendar end to end: budget and long-range planning milestones, forecast cycles, month-end and performance review inputs, orchestrating and collaborating so that every corporate deadline is met reliably and consistently.

• Own the reporting catalogue with clear service levels, and build the automation toolchain that produces the recurring suite, retiring manual production as you go.

**What Is Needed To Succeed

**

• 7-10 years in financial planning, reporting or control; you have run a planning calendar or close process end to end.

• At least one recurring reporting process you automated, with the manual version retired, and genuine energy for doing it again at scale.

**Who You Are

jobs.description:
Do you want to lead the ecological interpretation of complex offshore bird-monitoring projects? Can you turn radar, video, acoustic and environmental data into scientifically defensible conclusions for clients and regulators? Join DHI and take scientific ownership of projects at the intersection of avian ecology, technology and offshore wind.

Responsibilities and challenges

We are looking for a Biologist to support the scientific delivery of DHI MUSE and avian ecology projects. You will contribute to biological reviews, ecological analyses, reporting, and project coordination, working with experienced biologists, data scientists, instrumentation specialists and project managers. You will take increasing ownership of routine project-level scientific tasks, with guidance from senior colleagues and the Scientific Lead.

Your main responsibilities and challenges will include:

• Prepare, organise and analyse radar, video, acoustic, weather and system-status data needed for scientific deliverables.

• Contribute to ecological analyses of flight trajectories, bird flux, species distribution, phenology, avoidance behaviour and collision risk.

• Work with data scientists and analysts to review results and interpret them in their ecological context.

• Draft report sections, technical notes, presentations, figures, tables and responses to review comments.

• Document assumptions, uncertainty, limitations and other performance aspects clearly and consistently.

• Participate in project meetings and support communication with clients, suppliers, subcontractors and other DHI teams.

• Follow approved methods and quality procedures, and escalate unsupported conclusions or non-standard methods to senior colleagues.

Qualifications and personal skills

We are looking for a colleague with the following qualifications:

Required:

• Master's degree in biology, ecology, ornithology or a closely related discipline, equivalent relevant qualifications or other proven merits and references in ornithology.

• A strong foundation in avian ecology, species identification, animal behaviour, migration ecology or environmental monitoring.

• Ability to analyse scientific information and communicate findings clearly in writing and orally.

• Careful and consistent approach to biological classification, quality assurance and documentation.

• Good data-handling skills and willingness to work with radar, video, acoustic and environmental datasets.

• Excellent written and spoken English.

• Ability to collaborate across biological, analytical, technical and project-management disciplines.

• Ability to use AI to speed up delivery without loss of quality.

Desirable:

• Relevant professional, internship, thesis or research experience in bird monitoring, ecological consultancy or offshore wind.

• Experience reviewing wildlife video or acoustic recordings, identifying birds, or working with behavioural annotations.

• Experience in R, Python or other tools used for data analysis.

• Knowledge of environmental impact assessment, collision-risk modelling or remote-sensing methods.

Personal qualities:

• Curious, methodical and keen to learn.

• Self-motivated and comfortable asking for guidance when needed.

• Strong attention to detail and scientific integrity.

• Collaborative, service-minded and able to communicate with colleagues from different disciplines.

We offer

To work at DHI means being part of an organisation that addresses complex challenges in water and the environment. We will offer you:

• A role where ecological science is applied directly to offshore wind and environmental decision-making.

• Collaboration with biologists, data scientists, analysts, instrumentation specialists and project managers.

• Professional and personal development, with room to grow your scientific and client-facing responsibilities.

• Flexible working opportunities.

• A diverse, international network of highly skilled colleagues.

• The opportunity to contribute to the continued development of DHI MUSE and avian ecology services.

About DHI and DHI MUSE

DHI is a global and independent company dedicated to working on challenges within the fields of water and environment and sustainability. Within these fields, we provide a wide range of advisory, digital advisory, research and water governance services as well as providing leading edge MIKE and MUSE technologies and products to the market. At DHI, we are constantly looking for passionate and talented people who are eager to join our team.

By joining DHI, you will not only become part of a dynamic and collaborative global team of experts; you will be empowered to innovate, engage and grow in your area of expertise. DHI is committed to disseminate our knowledge effectively and across our worldwide network of offices.

• Please submit your application and CV via the relevant job posting on DHI Careers.

jobs.occupation: Interdisciplinary Postdoctoral Fellow in Host-Directed Antimicrobial Research
jobs.description:
We are looking for a highly motivated and dynamic postdoc for a one-year position to commence 1 March 2027 or after agreement.

  Introduction

  Antimicrobial resistance is a growing global health challenge that highlights the need for innovative therapeutic strategies beyond conventional antibiotic treatment.

  Host-directed antimicrobial strategies are attracting increasing interest as complementary approaches to conventional antimicrobial therapy. Recent studies have demonstrated that a novel synthetic compound improves survival in methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA)-infected Caenorhabditis elegans. Furthermore, previous studies in mammalian cells suggest that the compound may exert immunomodulatory effects, raising the possibility that stimulation of host defence pathways contributes to protection against infection.

  This project aims to determine whether the novel synthetic compound can stimulate innate immunity and enhance host defence pathways in C. elegans and thereby contribute to protection against MRSA-infection. Using a combination of immunology, microbiology, and transcriptomics, the successful candidate will lead the experimental investigation of the phenotypic and transcriptional responses underlying this protective effect. All experimental work will be conducted in C. elegans.

  Required qualifications

   	
• A PhD in immunology, infection biology, microbiology, molecular biology, biomedical sciences, pharmacology, or a related discipline. 	
• Hands-on experience with the maintenance and experimental use of Caenorhabditis elegans, preferably as an infection model. 	
• Knowledge to innate immunity and host defence pathways. 	
• Demonstrated ability to conduct independent research. 	
• Excellent written and oral communication skills in English.   Highly desirable qualifications

   	
• Knowledge to innate immunity and host defence pathways in Caenorhabditis elegans. 	
• Experience with bacterial culture and experimental microbiology. 	
• Experience with omics-data analysis (such as RNA-seq data). 	
• Experience with quantitative PCR (qPCR) and gene expression analysis. 	
• Experience with RNA interference (RNAi) and gene-silencing approaches. 	
• Knowledge of antimicrobial compounds and antimicrobial resistance. 	
• Experience contributing to external funding applications. 	
• A strong publication record relative to career stage.   Key responsibilities

  The postdoctoral fellow will conduct research within host-directed antimicrobial strategies and innate immunity. The successful candidate is expected to contribute to student supervision, assist in the preparation of external funding applications, and lead the dissemination of research findings through scientific publications and presentations, as well as participate in other academic activities.

  Research environment and collaboration 

  The successful candidate will be based in a research environment with expertise in C. elegans biology and will interact closely with collaborators possessing complementary expertise in immunity, microbiology, and bioinformatics. The interdisciplinary nature of the project provides excellent opportunities for scientific exchange and the development of skills across multiple disciplines while independently driving the research project.

  Further information

  Further information on the Department is linked at https://ivh.ku.dk/. Inquiries about the position can be made to Associate Professor Tina V. A. Hansen, alstrup@sund.ku.dk

  Starting date and duration

  The position is available from 1 March 2027 or after agreement. The position is a fixed-term, full-time postdoctoral appointment for a period of one year.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  Please include

• Research plan – description of current and future research plans 	
• Complete publication list 	
• Separate reprints of 3 particularly relevant papers 	
• Contact information for 2–3 references.   The deadline for applications is Tuesday 24 November 2026, 23:59pm CET

Once the assessment work has been completed each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself.

The Department of Anthropology, School of Culture and Society, invites applications for a three-year position as assistant professor in relation to the research project “Stories from my new life: Mobile transitions and social becomings among resettled refugees in Denmark” (TRANSIT).

An assistant professorship is a full-time, three-year training position that involves research and teaching at the BA and MA level and includes an obligatory course in university teaching for assistant professors. The position will commence on 1 February, 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. 

Place of employment: Department of Anthropology, Moesgaard Allé 20, 8270 Højbjerg, Denmark.

The Faculty of Arts is committed to creating an inclusive working environment and therefore encourages all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of personal background, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, ethnicity etc.

The position
The position will be associated with the research project TRANSIT at the Department of Anthropology and is a combined teaching and research position.

Here is a brief description of the TRANSIT project:

In 2021-2024 app. 600 Congolese women and children were resettled in Denmark under the UNHCR resettlement program. TRANSIT is concerned with resettled refugees’ life transitions, understood as a set of complex legal, social and existential transitions that are particularly urgent in the context of resettlement: 1) the transition from youth to adulthood; 2) the transition from being single to being married; and 3) the transition into old age and, ultimately, death. The project aims to establish a collaboration between Aarhus University, VIVE – The Danish Center for Social Science Research, FLUGT – Refugee Museum of Denmark, DFUNK – Dansk Flygtningehjælp Ungdom and a large group of resettled families in order to: a) create a mobile pop-up exhibition to be presented across Denmark in 2029; b) develop research-based teaching materials for pupils in the final years of Folkeskolen and in Gymnasiet on what it means to be resettled and start a new life in Denmark; and c) publish articles in leading peer-reviewed journals – based on a range of qualitative and quantitative data – on storytelling and life transitions following resettlement.

The selected candidate is expected to do individual fieldwork, be main responsible for a work-package (developing research-based teaching material with FLUGT – Refugee Museum of Denmark), and to be a dedicated member of the project team and engaged in all the project activities and responsibilities.

The position is offered with a view to attracting qualified applicants with an established and well-documented research record in innovative and internationally recognized research within anthropology and a specialization in migration and refugee studies, collaborative methods and creative forms of research dissemination. 

Research
The selected applicant will be expected to contribute to core activities at the School of Culture and Society and Aarhus University in general and contribute to the Department of Anthropology’s research activities and output in particular. They will be expected to take an interest in interdisciplinary research collaboration within the Department of Anthropology, the School of Culture and Society, the Faculty of Arts, and beyond. 

The selected applicant will also be expected to develop new research projects with internal and external partners and to raise external research funding. The applicant’s research credentials and publication record within the field, e.g. anthropology, migration and refugee studies, collaborative methods and creative forms of research dissemination, will be assessed not just on existing publications and other research contributions but also on research potential.

Past research output will be assessed based on the active research time of the applicant in question. We therefore ask applicants to specify any career breaks they have had (for instance due to maternity/paternity leave or sick leave) so we may discount these periods when assessing research productivity.

Teaching
The position will involve some teaching (up to 33% of the time) as agreed upon with the Head of the Department and the project PI. The selected applicant will be required to teach and supervise at BA and MA levels of the department’s degree programs in Anthropology and Human Security and will be expected to have teaching experience at university level. 

We emphasise the importance of maintaining a professional and respectful relationship between staff and students, so applicants should be able to demonstrate and exemplify their commitment to participatory teaching initiatives and student involvement as part of their teaching portfolio.

Qualifications
Applicants must hold a PhD or equivalent qualifications in anthropology or a related discipline. They must also be able to document the following: 

• An internationally oriented research profile documented through relevant academic publications, and possibly other research contributions, at the international level
• Experience of university-level teaching and a commitment to teaching development and the supervision of student projects
• Experience of or interest in active participation in international research collaboration
• Experience of or interest in obtaining external research funding
• Experience of or interest in research dessimination for a non-academic audience

• A full publication list (research outputs and public dissemination)

Only submitted publications will be assessed; a list of publications is not sufficient. As a result, applications without submitted publications will not be assessed.

References or recommendations should not be included with the application. Applicants who are selected for a job interview may be asked to provide professional references.

Applicants should document any prior experience within the field of knowledge exchange.

Our work examines how people interact with their environments, from prehistory to the present and across both local and global contexts. Through cross-sector and cross-disciplinary partnerships, we aim to support research innovation and contribute to addressing the major questions facing society.
